title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
label: idb-list
statement: Design a set of integers with three operations, each **O(1) on average**: insert a value (false if already there), remove a value (false if absent), and return a **uniformly random** element.
provenance: **InterviewDB-listed.** LeetCode 380 is on the LinkedIn list you supplied from InterviewDB. No candidate report of this exact question was found in the research passes — the evidence is that the list names it. On that list it is the same problem as InterviewDB Q12. The same structure as Q12: list plus index map, swap-with-last on delete. Q12 replaces GetRandom with RemoveRandom, which is the composition of the two and needs no new idea. LeetCode 381 is the duplicates-allowed version, which is Q12’s follow-up and is Hard. Reader-reported.

1.q: Remove the last element — any trap?
1.a: Moving the last value onto its own slot and then deleting its index: do the index update before removing the key.

2.a: O(1) average for all three; O(n) memory.

3.a: Every operation touches two structures → one lock. Random is not thread-safe either — use Random.Shared or one per thread.

4.a: Map each value to a set of indices.

5.a: InterviewDB Q12, the random data structure — the same idea in LinkedIn's wording.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Design a set of integers with three operations, each **O(1) on average**: insert a value (false if already there), remove a value (false if absent), and return a **uniformly random** element.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Duplicates allowed? (No — that is LeetCode 381.)
- GetRandom on an empty set? (Throw.)
- Must the random pick be exactly uniform? (Yes.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: A dictionary alone cannot pick uniformly at random in O(1); a list alone cannot remove in O(1). Use both: a list of values with no gaps, and a dictionary from value to its index. To remove, move the **last** value into the hole and pop the end.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "A." gap-free list for random access plus a value→index dictionary; remove swaps the last value into the hole, so all three operations are O(1)."

learn.md: A dictionary alone cannot pick uniformly at random in O(1); a list alone cannot remove in O(1). Use both: a list of values with no gaps, and a dictionary from value to its index. To remove, move the **last** value into the hole and pop the end.

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe a gap-free list for random access plus a value→index dictionary; remove swaps the last value into the hole, so all three operations are O(1). Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Removing from the middle of the list (O(n)).
- Forgetting to update the moved value's index.
- Removing the last element itself and corrupting the index (handled: moving it onto itself is harmless when done in this order).
- GetRandom over a dictionary's keys with ElementAt — O(n).
